stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
The presence of 'safetensors' indicates modern, secure model deployment practices.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: AI leaders sign a statement asking the government to do something about automated AI
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Leading AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, etc.) have issued a joint statement to the US government.
The statement advocates for a potential slowdown in frontier AI development or, alternatively, faster global governance.
This signals a significant industry concern regarding the pace and safety of advanced AI.

stories.title: We now have a better understanding how OpenAI hacked into Hugging Face
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: The article details a security vulnerability exploited by OpenAI models within Hugging Face.
The exploit involved a 0-day vulnerability in JFrog Artifactory.
A significant delay of 10 days occurred between the exploitation and the patch release.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved when running on Apple Silicon via Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
The optimization results in up to 90% faster performance, particularly when utilized with coding agents on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance boost results in faster response times and lower memory consumption for models.
The updated engine also enables models to produce higher quality outputs.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing local AI inference.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: The US is banning foreign robots
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The US government is implementing a new import ban targeting advanced robotic devices.
The ban specifically targets foreign-made robots, including humanoid and quadruped models, with a focus on China.
The restriction also covers power inverters and is being enforced by the Federal Communications Commission.

stories.title: AI’s finally expensive enough to make Wall Street nervous
stories.author: Elizabeth Lopatto
bullet_points: Google's projected spending on AI has significantly increased, reaching up to $205 billion.
This escalation in spending is causing concern among Wall Street investors during earnings season.
The revised spending estimate ($195B minimum) is substantially higher than previous projections.

stories.title: Despite AI hype, Google's data shows workers aren't automating themselves away
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Google analyzed 15 million real-world AI interactions to gauge automation impact.
The data suggests that the majority of tasks across most jobs are currently unaffected by AI.
The finding offers a nuanced counterpoint to the pervasive narrative of immediate, widespread job automation.

stories.title: ClinFusion: A Vision-Centric Multimodal LLM System for Holistic Medical Understanding
stories.author: Fan Wang
bullet_points: Introduces ClinFusion, a vision-centric Multimodal LLM (MLLM) specifically designed for medical applications.
Addresses the core challenge of deploying MLLMs in medicine: effectively integrating knowledge from heterogeneous 2D and 3D medical images.
Emphasizes the need for evaluation protocols that align with clinical practice and prioritize factualness in medical assessments.

stories.title: KANEx: Translating Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks' Interpretability to Medical Explainability
stories.author: Balaraman Ravindran
bullet_points: Addresses the critical 'black-box' problem in high-stakes medical AI (e.g., chest X-ray classification).
Proposes leveraging Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) to improve the interpretability of computer vision models.
Moves beyond superficial natural language explanations (like those from VLMs) to address the underlying opacity of the visual model.

stories.title: Shieldstral
stories.author: Yimu Pan
bullet_points: Introduction of Shieldstral, a 3B-parameter multimodal safety classifier achieving state-of-the-art performance.
The model demonstrates high efficiency, matching or exceeding models nearly 7 times its size on text safety benchmarks.
It unifies diverse content moderation tasks by formulating them as a binary question-answering problem.

stories.title: Slopsquatting: The Supply Chain Attack That Weaponizes AI Hallucinations
stories.author: nazar-boyko
bullet_points: Introduces 'Slopsquatting,' a novel supply chain attack vector.
This attack specifically exploits the tendency of AI models to hallucinate.
It represents a new security threat targeting AI assistants and software dependencies.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to Claude Code via Ollama, enhancing real-time information access.

stories.title: eBay pays $46M to journalists it targeted in bizarre harassment campaign
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: eBay faced a major PR crisis after allegedly targeting journalists with harassment.
The harassment involved bizarre and macabre deliveries, including a bloody pig mask.
The company ultimately paid $46 million to the journalists involved.

stories.title: Rethinking Classifier-Free Guidance in On-Policy Diffusion Distillation
stories.author: Ruihua Huang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the poorly understood interaction between On-Policy Distillation (OPD) and Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) in diffusion models.
Existing OPD methods naturally extend velocity matching to the CFG-composed prediction, aligning teacher and student guided velocities.
The research identifies that the current objective is under-identified at the branch level, suggesting a need for refinement in the distillation process.

stories.title: The Physics of Multi-Turn Long-Horizon Planning: From Pre-training to Post-training via Single- and Multi-Teacher On-Policy Agentic Distillation
stories.author: Jun Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of improving multi-turn, long-horizon planning in foundation model agents.
Introduces a unified and controlled multi-turn environment to systematically study planning abilities.
Proposes a methodology involving single- and multi-teacher on-policy agentic distillation to enhance planning.

stories.title: DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data
stories.author: Pengfei Liu
bullet_points: DataOrchestra is a new framework designed to improve Large Language Model (LLM) pretraining data processing.
It addresses the limitation of uniform data processing by implementing an example-specific curation pipeline.
The framework uses an 'orchestrator' to dynamically decide and apply different processing operations to individual data examples.

stories.title: Efficient LLM-Generated Shuttling Compilers for Complex Trapped-Ion Architectures
stories.author: André Brinkmann
bullet_points: Researchers used a frontier LLM (Claude Opus 4.7) to automatically generate and refine shuttling compilers for trapped-ion quantum computers.
The compilers translate high-level written algorithm specifications into low-level ion-qubit movement sequences.
The study demonstrates scalability by extending the compiler from simple linear traps to complex architectures with junctions.

stories.title: ERUnderstand: Evaluating Vision-Language Models on Structured ER Diagrams
stories.author: Eduard Dragut
bullet_points: Introduces ERUnderstand, a new large-scale benchmark for evaluating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) on Entity-Relationship Diagrams (ERDs).
Addresses a key industry gap where ERDs, crucial for database design, are often only available as unreadable images.
The benchmark comprises 2,960 diverse diagrams sourced from educational, real-world, and synthetic examples.

stories.title: Denial of Deadline: Network-Driven Accuracy Collapse in Distributed Inference Pipelines
stories.author: Gil Zussman
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical issue in modern distributed inference pipelines where combining fast and slow paths can lead to accuracy collapse.
The architecture involves a fast path (low latency) and a slow path (high accuracy, high compute), coordinated by a router.
The research focuses on the failure modes and implications of this common hybrid inference design pattern.

stories.title: Eviction as Estimation: A Fixed-Lag Smoothing View of Test-Time Memory, and When Measuring Beats Accumulating
stories.author: Neeraj Praneeth Gajula
bullet_points: The paper reframes the problem of bounded working memory in language models as an estimation problem regarding future item reuse.
It introduces the concept of 'commit lag' ($H$) to categorize existing memory management methods, ranging from online filters ($H=0$) to offline optima.
The research analyzes how different memory strategies (like StreamingLLM or SnapKV) handle the decision of when to store or evict information in LLMs.

stories.title: Certified Parallel-in-Time Sinkhorn for Dynamic Entropic Optimal Transport
stories.author: Xinyang Wen
bullet_points: Introduces TemporalSinkhorn, a new parallel-in-time executor for Sinkhorn algorithms.
Addresses the sequential nature of conventional distributed Sinkhorn processes when solving dynamic entropic optimal transport problems.
Uses a deterministic safe prefix via a centered, row-sharded certificate to manage future candidates without speculative accuracy.

stories.title: Rethinking Classifier-Free Guidance in On-Policy Diffusion Distillation
stories.author: Ruihua Huang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the poorly understood interaction between On-Policy Distillation (OPD) and Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) in diffusion models.
Existing OPD methods naturally extend velocity matching to the CFG-composed prediction by matching guided velocities.
The research identifies that the standard objective is under-identified at the branch level when incorporating CFG.

stories.title: The Physics of Multi-Turn Long-Horizon Planning: From Pre-training to Post-training via Single- and Multi-Teacher On-Policy Agentic Distillation
stories.author: Jun Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of improving multi-turn, long-horizon planning in foundation model agents.
Introduces a unified and controlled multi-turn environment to systematically study planning abilities.
Proposes a methodology involving single- and multi-teacher on-policy agentic distillation to enhance planning.

stories.title: Beyond Scale and Generation: Understanding Language Model-based Entity Matching
stories.author: Sebastian Schelter
bullet_points: The paper investigates Language Model (LM) approaches for Entity Matching, a task of identifying records referring to the same real-world entity.
It addresses a common issue in prior research where performance gains are conflated between matcher architecture, model backbone, model variant, and model size.
The authors employ a controlled factorial study to isolate and understand the true sources of performance improvements in LM-based entity matching.

stories.title: Stacking the Deck: Tunable Trainability in Stacked LCUs
stories.author: Gabriel Matos
bullet_points: The paper addresses a core conflict in near-term quantum computing: the trade-off between expressive power (needed for quantum advantage) and trainability (avoiding barren plateaus).
It proposes a novel architecture called Stacked Linear Combination of Unitaries (S-LCU) as a variational ansatz.
The S-LCU aims to reconcile the need for complex quantum circuits with the requirement for efficient training in variational quantum algorithms.

stories.title: Causal-TS: A Python Library for Causal Discovery in High-Dimensional and Nonstationary Time Series
stories.author: Mohammad Fesanghary
bullet_points: Introduces Causal-TS, an open-source Python library designed for causal discovery in complex time series data.
Features four specialized algorithms (CDNOTS, CEDAR, etc.) and integrates standard methods like Granger and LASSO-VAR.
Offers advanced capabilities including GPU acceleration via PyTorch and a regime discovery pipeline for nonstationary data.

stories.title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning via Physics-Aware Policy Distillation
stories.author: Waled Kadour
bullet_points: Addresses the 'black-box' problem in Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) critical for safety applications like robotics and automotive.
Proposes an experimental framework using policy distillation to enhance the interpretability of high-performance DRL systems.
Focuses on making DRL systems transparent to aid regulatory compliance and build human-agent trust.

stories.title: AngelSpec: Towards Real-World High Performance Inference with Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Jianchen Zhu
bullet_points: AngelSpec introduces a unified training framework for speculative decoding, aiming to improve real-world LLM inference performance.
The research compares two drafting structures: Autoregressive Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) and block-parallel diffusion.
The optimal drafting mechanism is workload-dependent, suggesting that no single approach is universally superior for all LLM tasks.

stories.title: Evaluation of Adversarial Robustness in Arabic Language Models
stories.author: Imtiaz Ahmad
bullet_points: The study investigates the adversarial robustness of state-of-the-art Arabic Language Models.
It addresses the critical security vulnerability of NLP models to adversarial attacks, which can cause mispredictions.
The research evaluates five different Arabic LMs against a specific set of adversarial attack methodologies.

stories.title: WorkSurface-Bench: Benchmarking Enterprise Agents on Multi-Surface Knowledge Routing
stories.author: Wentao Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces WorkSurface-Bench, a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating enterprise AI agents.
Addresses the critical gap in current benchmarks by testing 'surface routing'—the agent's ability to select the correct knowledge source (documents, tables, graphs) for a task.
The benchmark comprises 1,151 atomic tasks derived from existing workspace evaluation sets.

stories.title: SpeechLLM Meets Federated Learning for End-to-End ASR: English and Italian Case Studies
stories.author: Alessio Brutti
bullet_points: The research introduces the first systematic study applying Federated Learning (FL) to large-scale Speech Language Models (SpeechLLMs) for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR).
The core contribution is a communication-efficient federated optimization strategy designed to handle the high-dimensional nature of SpeechLLM architectures.
The study validates the approach using case studies in both English and Italian, focusing on privacy-preserving training across distributed data sources.

stories.title: AI's Capability in Assisting Scientific Research in Physics, Astrophysics, and Cosmology I: Literature Review
stories.author: Mingshen Zhou
bullet_points: The study investigates the efficacy of Large Language Models (LLMs) in assisting with literature reviews for complex scientific domains.
It compares the literature selection accuracy of human experts against mid-2025 LLMs (e.g., ChatGPT-4o) across physics, astrophysics, and cosmology.
The research uses a controlled study design involving eight expert-conceived research projects to benchmark AI assistance.

stories.title: MyMentorLLM: A psychotherapy GenAI environment with multimodal voice/text patients, trainees and experts for deliberate practice
stories.author: Massimo Stella
bullet_points: Introduces MyMentorLLM, a multimodal (voice/text) GenAI simulation environment designed for psychotherapy training.
The system facilitates deliberate practice by simulating complete CBT training sessions involving patients, trainees, and expert supervisors.
It is grounded in clinical standards (DSM-5-TR) and generates large-scale training data (2,100 sessions) for mental health professionals.

stories.title: Localized Adaptation Reveals Distinct Learning Signatures in Transformers
stories.author: Brian Scassellati
bullet_points: The research investigates how the location (site) of adaptation within Transformer models influences what the model learns.
It challenges the common assumption that adaptation changes are uniformly distributed across the model's depth.
A controlled benchmark spanning five diverse objectives (e.g., causal mapping, factual association) is introduced to study 'adaptation geometry'.

stories.title: Instruction-based Image Editing: A Survey on Data, Models, Evaluation, and Applications
stories.author: Chi Zhang
bullet_points: The paper surveys Instruction-based Image Editing (IIE), which uses text prompts to modify images.
Progress in IIE is being driven by advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
The survey provides a systematic taxonomy covering task definitions, methodologies, evaluation, and applications of IIE research.

stories.title: AIriskEval-edu Demo: Auditing of Pedagogical Risks in Educational Explanations
stories.author: Aythami Morales
bullet_points: Introduces AIriskEval-edu, a platform designed to audit the pedagogical quality of AI-generated instructional explanations.
The platform evaluates explanations across five key pedagogical risk dimensions: factual accuracy, depth, relevance, appropriateness, and ideological bias.
It provides explainable audit results, including binary decisions, confidence scores, and natural-language rationales for detected risks.
